articleTitle: The hodge numbers of the moduli spaces of vector bundles over a Riemann surface
A Rate Estimate in Billingsleys Theorem for the Size Distribution of Large Prime Factors
The Diophantine equation d2x4 + 1 = Dy2
abstract: For given d and D, an effective method is derived for completely solving the equation in the title in positive integers x and y.

articleTitle: Stable Pairs and Principal Bundles
abstract: A general equation, for a pair (A, Φ), where Ais a connection on a principal bundle and Φa section of an associated bundle, is studied. It is shown how it includes the case of Higgs bundles, the Vafa–Witten equation and others.

articleTitle: An elementary proof of the ‘strange formula’ of freudenthal and de vries
Optimality of embeddings of logarithmic Bessel potential spaces
abstract: We establish the sharpness of recently-obtained embedding theorems for certain logarithmic Bessel potential spaces modelled upon generalized Lorentz-Zygmund (GLZ) spaces. The target spaces may be of GLZ or Hölder type, including in particular spaces of 'almost Lipschitz' type familiar from the work of Brézis and Wainger.

articleTitle: Unstable multiplicative cohomology operations
abstract: We investigate the relationship between multiplicative unstable cohomology operations G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(−) → E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(−)and formal group laws for a certain important class of theories. As an application we study additive multiplicative idempotents.

articleTitle: Normal Forms for Automorphisms of Maximal Rank
abstract: In this paper we show that maximal rank automorphisms of free groups have a solvable conjugacy problem by using combinatorial methods. Combined with the results from D. J. Collins and E. C. Turner (1996) All automorphisms of free groups with maximal rank fixed subgroups Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 119no. 4, 615–630, this gives a normal form for such automorphisms. We also show that it is possible to algorithmically find the fixed subgroup of a maximal rank automorphism.

articleTitle: Unstable splittings of classifying spaces of P-compact groups
abstract: Dwyer and Wilkerson gave a definition of a p-compact group, which is a loop space with certain properties and a good generalization of the notion of compact Lie groups in terms of classifying spaces and homotopy theory; e.g. every p-compact group has a maximal torus, a normalizer of the maximal torus and a Weyl group. The belief or hope that p-compact groups enjoy most properties of compact Lie groups establishes a program for the classification of these objects. Following the classification of compact connected Lie groups, one step in this program is to show that every simply connected p-compact group splits into a product of simply connected simple p-compact groups. The proof of this splitting theorem is based on the fact that every classifying space of a p-compact group splits into a product if the normalizer of the maximal torus does.

articleTitle: Proof of a weak hyperbolization theorem
abstract: We sketch a new proof of a consequence of Thurston’s Uniformization Theorem which asserts that atoroidal Haken 3-manifolds have word hyperbolic fundamental groups. The proof uses the Combination Theorem of Bestvina and Feighn, a new quasiconvexity criterion and standard 3-manifold techniques.

articleTitle: Almost Kähler 4-manifolds with J-invariant ricci tensor and special weyl tensor
abstract: We give topological conditions for the existence of almost Kähler 4-manifolds with certain curvature properties.

articleTitle: Interiority of real functions
abstract: Conditions concerning openness of continuous real functions defined on topological spaces are studied. It is shown that for locally compact metrizable spaces interiority of the function at a point is equivalent to having no local extremum at this point if and only if the domain space is connected im kleinen at the point. Some related results are some obtained and open questions are posed.

articleTitle: Biquasitriangular Operators have Strongly Irreducible Perturbations
abstract: We prove that if T is a biquasitriangular operator on a Hilbert space H with connected spectrum then T may be approximated by a strongly irreducible operator S with S-T compact and small.

articleTitle: Neumann laplacians on domains and operators on associated trees
abstract: Connections are established between the essential specta of the Neumann Laplacian on a domain Ω in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a one-term operator of Sturm–Liouville type which is defined naturally on the skeleton, or a generalized ridge, Γ of Ω, when Γ is a tree. Horns, spirals, ‘rooms and passages’ and domains with fractal boundaries, like the Koch snowflake, are examples of such domains Ω. The analysis hinges on the existence of isometric maps between L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Ω), H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(Ω) and weighted L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> spaces defined on Γ in terms of a Lipschitz map τ which projects Ω onto Γ.

articleTitle: Weighted inequalities for Bochner-Riesz means in the plane
abstract: We give weighted inequalities for Bochner-Riesz means and the corresponding maximal operator in the plane. These capture the known L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sup> results for these operators simultaneously for all values of q < 2. The sharp L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> estimate for the natural square function associated to the problem is also obtained.

articleTitle: New bounds for Gauss sums derived from KTH powers, and for Heilbronn's exponential sum
abstract: We show that p/Σ/n=1 exp (2π ian<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>/p) << min (k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/8</sup>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,8</sup>, k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/8</sup>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/4</sup>and p/Σ/n=1 exp (2π ian<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>/p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) << p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/8</sup> when p Xa. The proof uses a modification of Stepanov's method.

articleTitle: Remarques sur les théorèmes d'immersion de Hahn et Hausdorff et sur les corps de séries formelles
abstract: We give a short proof of the Hausdorff-Sierpinski embedding theorem for linearly ordered sets and of the existence of inverses for nonzero elements of Hahn's rings of formal series. We also give a new proof and an improved version of Hahn's embedding theorem for linearly ordered groups.

articleTitle: Some Sums of Two Rational Cubes
abstract: This paper establishes the result that numbers of the shape 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>p(p ≡ 2 mod9)and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(p ≡ 5 mod9), where pa prime, are expressible as the sum of two rational cubes by finding modular parametrizations of the corresponding elliptic curves, picking special complex points on the curve and manipulating them to produce rational points thereon.

articleTitle: Verbal subgroups in residually finite groups
abstract: For certain family of group words wwe prove that if qis a prime-power, and if Gis a residually finite group in which any w-value has order dividing qthen the corresponding verbal subgroup w(G)is locally finite.

articleTitle: Absolutely irreducible finitary skew linear groups
abstract: We introduce a notion of absolute irreducibility for finitary skew linear groups consistent with the existing notions for finite-dimensional linear groups, finite-dimensional skew linear groups and finitary linear groups and then prove some relatively strong results about such absolutely irreducible groups.

articleTitle: Invariant Laminations for Diffeomorphisms of Handlebodies
abstract: We study diffeomorphisms of handelbodies from the point of view of invariant laminations.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of the cauchy transform in L2(C, dμ)
abstract: The exact asymptotic of the singular values of the Cauchy transform C over the space L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(C, dμ)and the estimate of the singular values of the operator PC are obtained, where P is the Bargman projection.

articleTitle: The Cherry Transform and its Relationship with a Singular Sturm–liouville Problem
abstract: A Plancherel-type theorem is established in two ways for the Cherry transform.

articleTitle: Trace scaling automorphisms of certain stable AF algebras II
abstract: Two automorphisms of a simple stable AF-algebra with a finite dimensional lattice of lower semicontinuous traces are shown to be outer conjugate if they act in the same way on K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and the extremal traces are scaled by numbers which are not equal to 1 and satisfy a certain condition (which holds if the scaling factors are all less than 1). The proof goes via the Rohlin property. As an application we consider the problem of classifying conjugacy or cocycle conjugacy classes of certain actions of T on a separable simple purely infinite C*-algebra.

articleTitle: The least common multiple and lattice points on hyperbolas
abstract: We bound, from below, the least common multiple of k integers from a short interval. This is used to bound the length of an arc Γ of the hyperbola, xy = N, containing k integer lattice points.

articleTitle: Cohomology and induction from elementary Abelian subgroups
abstract: In this paper we present a general view of the role of elementary Abelian subgroups in the representation theory of a finite group G. We show that any G-module M is a direct summand of a module that has a filtration by modules induced from elementary Abelian subgroups. This implies that if we are given any sequence of cohomology elements, such that the product of the elements in the sequence makes sense and that the elements restrict to zero on the elementary Abelian subgroups, then the product of the elements is zero provided the sequence has sufficient length. If the coefficient ring is a field of finite characteristic p, then only the elementary Abelian p-subgroups are relevant. In that case, the theorems of Quillen on the dimension of the mod-p cohomology ring and of Alperin-Evens on the complexity of modules are easy consequences of our results.

articleTitle: Finding measures with given marginals
abstract: Let (A, X)and (B, Y)be measurable spaces and let Vbe a Dedekind σ-complete vector lattice. Let μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>and μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>be measures defined on Aand B, respectively, and taking their values in the positive cone of V. We define σ-additivity of V-valued measures with respect to the order structure of V. Let A[otimes]Bbe the σ-field generated by Aand B. It is shown here that classical results of Strassen can be generalized to this situation. In particular, when μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(X) = μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(Y), there exists a V-valued σ-additive measure μon A[otimes]Bsuch that μ(A× Y) = μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(A)and μ(X ×B) = μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(B)if μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>is σ-additive, μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>is σ-compact and Vsatisfies the lattice condition of being weakly σ-distributive. When Vis Dedekind complete and satisfies the stronger property of weak (σ, ∞)-distributivity then analogous results hold with μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>satisfying the weaker property of being completely compact.

articleTitle: On the Isometry Groups of Cyclic Branched Coverings of Hyperbolic Knots
abstract: There is no general method for computing the isometry group of a given hyperbolic 3-manifold. We consider the case of a cyclic covering M of a hyperbolic knot K.

articleTitle: Investigation and Application of the Dressing Action on Surfaces of Constant Mean Curvature
abstract: We show in Theorem 1.5 that for immersions whose Hopf differential has zeroes, the isotropy group is trivial. In other words, the dressing action is simple on surfaces with umbilics.

articleTitle: Noether's Bound in the Invariant Theory of Finite Groups and Vector Invariants of Iterated Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
abstract: Let ρ : G ↪ GL(n, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex>) be a faithful representation of the finite group G over the field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex>. In 1916, E. Noether proved that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex> of characteristic zero the ring of invariants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex>[V]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup> is generated as an algebra by the invariant polynomials of degree at most |G|. This result has been generalized to the case where the characteristic of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex> is greater than |G|, or when the characteristic of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex> is prime to the order of G and the group G is solvable. In this note we show how to refine Noether's proof to yield a more general nonmodular result. In particular we prove that Noether's bound holds for the alternating groups in the nonmodular case.

articleTitle: High Order Smoothness and Roughness in Banach Spaces
abstract: We study the existence of equivalent norms nowhere k-times Fréchet differentiable (k ≥ 2) on Banach spaces, introducing the notion of high order roughness. We also study the existence of bump functions with high order Taylor expansions on subsymmetric spaces. Finally we prove that there is no uniformly twice Fréchet differentiable bump function on the 2-convexified Tsirelson space.

articleTitle: Gradient Comparison Theorems for Harmonic Functions on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Gradient comparison theorems are proved for positive bounded harmonic functions and positive eigenfunctions on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below. A characterization of the manifolds supporting extremal bounded harmonic or positive eigenfunctions is also given.

articleTitle: Subgroup Separability of Graphs of Free Groups with Cyclic Edge Groups
abstract: It is shown that π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of a finite graph of free groups with cyclic edge groups is subgroup separable unless π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> has a non-trivial element g such that g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> ∼ g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> with n ≠ ±m. It is easy to decide from the presentation if such a conjugacy exists.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Riemannian Metrics, Kähler-Einstein Metrics on Grauert Tubes and Harmonic Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: We characterize harmonic Riemannian manifolds in terms of the existence of special potentials for Kähler-Eintein metrics on (an open set) in their associated Grauert tubes, the potentials being solutions to an ODE on the canonical Monge-Ampère function. We establish a real version first, namely, special potentials for certain pseudo-Riemannian metrics, and analytically continue to the Grauert tube. We analyse the completeness of solutions for Damek-Ricci spaces.

articleTitle: On the Blocks of the Infinitesimal Schur Algebra
abstract: For a reductive algebraic group scheme G, much can be learnt about its representations over a field k of characteristic p > 0 by studying the representations of a related group scheme, G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>T, associated to the rth Frobenius kernel G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> and a maximal torus T of G. In the case G =GL(n, k) one can also consider the polynomial representations, and reduce to the study of representations of the Schur algebras. In [8] these two approaches were combined, and gave rise to the construction of a monoid scheme M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> D whose representations are equivalent to the polynomial representations of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>T. Just as in the ordinary case, this leads naturally to the study of certain finite dimensional algebras, the infinitesimal Schur algebras. In this paper we determine the blocks of these algebras when n = 2, which extends a result in [9] where the blocks were determined in the case n = 2 and r = 1. We conclude by defining a quantum version of the infinitesimal Schur algebras, and show that the corresponding result also holds in this case.
